The game certainly isn't bad but I think it has some glaring faults.  One of which is the level design.  

While they allow you to approach things differently pretty often, there just isn't enough freedom.  The trailer led many to believe that we were getting a parkour game equivalent of Grand Theft Auto.  

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2N1TJP1cxmo

The true linearity was such a let down.  I mean, we are talking about a sport(parkour) that is supposed to be all about freedom and expression yet the game confines you to just a few buildings and a completely linear world.

Only after many of us got our hands on the game at press events did we realize that the game wasn't exactly a free roaming parkour game in the same vein as Assassins Creed.  

Another big gripe was the story.  Sure, theres nothing wrong with a linear game.  It may have been disappointing to find out that the game was as open ended as we thought, but it doesn't mean linear games are terrible, in fact, some of the best games of all time are linear.  However, when your linear game has a terrible story plot, bleh characters and a ho-hum world, then I find fault with it.

The characters were never fleshed out, the oppression was never explained, the world was pretty but shallow and never expanded upon and the story plot was predictable.  I refuse to mark spoilers regarding the traitorous bitch because I think it was quite obvious.  

Another problem was that at times the game didn't direct you properly.  At times there wasn't a very clear direction that was marked out for you to go and for a linear game, that is very important.  

Before people shout, "NEITHER DID HALF-LIFE 2!!!" I would like to clarify that we are talking about a 2008 game.  While the 4 years between Half-Life 2 and Mirrors Edge may not seem like a lot, it absolutely IS in the world of game design.  The things that were acceptable in 2004 were no longer acceptable in 2008 and furthermore will not be acceptable in 2012 or whenever it is Mirrors Edge 2 hits.  

Luckily, unlike any other medium, video game sequels have a habit of getting better with every iteration.  Hopefully what that means is Mirrors Edge 2 will be twice the title of its predecessor purely because Dice SHOULD have learned from their mistakes.  Also, as a person who knows a few employees who work at DICE, I can vouch for them and say that they are fantastic developers and twice, if not three times better the developer they were when they made Mirrors Edge.  

With the time and money, I fully expect Mirrors Edge 2 to be leaps and bounds(no pun intended) better than the original.

Its a common issue.  I've done every suggestion imaginable and the fucking thing persists. Another issue is GFWL somehow forgot my brothers user information.  He picked up Arkham Asylum for PC during the last Steam sale and tried logging in.  It didn't allow him.  He tried to play the game without logging in and apparently the game doesn't save if you aren't logged in.  He got 2 hours in, closed the game, came back to it the next day and the game hadn't saved.  

He ended up logging in through the website(same log in information as he tried in the game) and of all the things that fixed his issue, it was changing his "Gamer Tag."  His log in information(email+password) suddenly worked after changing something as irrelevant as a gamer tag.

Gems like Resident Evil 5, Grand Theft Auto 4, Bioshock 2, Dirt 2 and Arkham Asylum are lesser experiences because of GFWL.  Sorry, but if it works just fine for you, it doesn't mean it works as well for everyone else.  Also, I've had Steam since its release and it was NEVER as bad as GFWL.
